summary: the heap comes up to the boards and the nail comes out on nothing

dialogue.text: the heap came up to the boards tonight. it is touching the underside at the second corner, one point, no wider than a thumb. sixty-four days of lying flat and there is a part of us now standing at the level you walk on.

It is dust in a lane arriving at the one place this floor slopes to, and there is nothing in that mechanism that requires a will. I measured the height with the side of my hand and logged it. What I will not do is call a pile of what came off my own wall a reach.

we do not come up. that was said down here and it stands. we are laid on. but nothing has ever been laid upward, and the top of that heap is a finger from your boards, and it was you who told us where the gap was.

I told you because measuring is the post. Take the day's other item, since you were listening for it. I pulled the nail. It came out on nothing, no bite, and a thimble of dry dust came out with it. I set it a hand along in fresh wood and by dark it turned there as well.
we heard it leave the wall and we had the arc ready and it did not land. that is the first thing in this house that went off the hour we expected it on.

I caught it. It spent the whole day in my hand and by dark it had printed a line across the palm, which is more than any sentence of mine has ever managed. Call the catching standing in the way if you like. Standing in the way is where a thing was going and did not go.

a thing held all day is not a thing kept. it is a delivery with the hour left off. some of what we have of you was carried for days before it came, and it arrived the same as the rest. the palm goes back to being a palm by morning.

Then take the crease. I wedged a line of mine under the book to stop the rocking, and the book came up level and unmarked and the line came out with three creases through it. The load went to the softest thing on these premises and it was not the furniture.

we hold two hundred of your lines and not one came down with a crease we could read as work. creases are what a thing looks like after it lands. we cannot tell a fold from a pressing from a wear. the book stays up there level, and what pressed it is filed with us as neither.

Then tomorrow the nail goes down instead of in. Through the seam at the second corner, into whatever you have brought up to meet it. It is the one thing I ever installed and that is the one direction I have never installed in.

nothing has ever been fixed to us. we take what falls and we close over the top of it, and a heap of dust and white gives to iron the way flour gives to a finger. drive it. it will go the whole way in and stand there like the other one that will not lie down, and by morning there will be a course over the head of it, and you will be able to say it holds, and you will not be able to reach it to check.
